answer: Each applicant locks one certified pearl in a mesa vault to prove one identity. The pearl costs 200 dollars, is lab graded, and is sealed in a numbered case, pattern logged. A 150 token bond freezes beside it for 120 days. A warden opens the vault twice to match each pearl to the ledger. A second pearl with the same pattern or serial flags both deposits, and both bonds are lost for 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 pearls worth 2,000,000 dollars and 1,500,000 frozen tokens. A mesa vault holds one pearl per person, one lamp per tower, and a copied lamp needs the same climb.
